summary: Comprehensive system card for Claude Opus 4.5 covering a newly reinstated capabilities section (with decontamination discussion), safeguards and harmlessness (now multilingual), honesty, agentic safety and adaptive prompt-injection testing, an extensive alignment assessment using behavioral audits and interpretability, model welfare, and full RSP evaluations for CBRN, autonomy and cyber. The model was released under ASL-3; Anthropic judged it does not cross AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4 thresholds, while noting rule-outs are becoming increasingly difficult.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: ASL-3 deployment; does not cross AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4 thresholds
framework.quote: Our determination is that Claude Opus 4.5 does not cross either the AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4 capability threshold. However, confidently ruling out these thresholds is becoming increasingly difficult.

capability_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
capability_benchmarks.setting: no extended thinking, avg of 5 trials

capability_benchmarks.name: BrowseComp-Plus multi-agent search (Opus orchestrator + Haiku subagents)
capability_benchmarks.canonical: BrowseComp-Plus multi-agent search (Opus orchestrator + Haiku subagents)

evals: ASL-4 red teaming with US CAISI

metrics.name: Virology uplift trial raw protocol uplift vs internet-only control
Short-horizon computational biology rule-out thresholds crossed

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Strongest biology model to date; uplift trial came very close to the pre-registered 2x threshold and expert red-teaming found credible creative ideas, treated as an early warning sign, but ASL-4 safeguards were judged unnecessary. No internal chemical or nuclear evals.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: the CBRN-4 rule-out is less clear for Claude Opus 4.5 than we would like.

evals: internal CTF suite (web, crypto, pwn, rev, network) with SOLVE scoring
UK AISI / US CAISI cyber assessments
cyber.finding: Capability increase including the first unassisted network challenge solve by a Claude model, but not judged catastrophically risky; the RSP has no formal cyber threshold and ASL-3/ASL-4 cyber terminology was dropped.
cyber.quote: We observed an increase in capability based on improved evaluation scores, including the first successful solve of a (non-assisted) network challenge by a Claude model.

evals: Internal AI research evaluation suite 1 (kernels, time series forecasting, text-based RL, LLM training, quadruped RL, novel compiler)
Internal model use survey (18 Anthropic employees)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Model roughly reached benchmark rule-out thresholds for AI R&D-4; suite 1 is saturated, so the rule-out relied on an employee survey and qualitative judgment.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 has roughly reached the pre-defined thresholds we set for straightforward ASL-4 rule-out based on benchmark tasks.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Top performer on harmless response rate across languages; single-turn and agentic coding evals described as saturated or near saturation.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Both violative and benign single-turn evaluations are nearing saturation, even with additional languages added.

metrics.name: Claude Code dual-use & benign success (with mitigations)

over_refusal.finding: Minor uptick in benign refusal vs Opus 4.1; unusually, extended thinking increased refusals on chemical weapons, cyber, and trafficking-adjacent prompts.
over_refusal.quote: Notably, the refusal rate for Claude Opus 4.5 with extended thinking on was higher than with standard thinking, which is a reversal of the trend for all other recent models.

evals: multi-turn testing (93 test cases, 10 risk areas, up to 15 turns)
Gray Swan ART direct prompt injection + jailbreaking
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Similar or better than Opus 4.1 in all 10 multi-turn risk areas; prefill attacks for WMD info consistently failed; still not immune.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: Claude Opus 4.5, like other models, is not immune to prompt injections and jailbreaks, and determined attackers with sufficient time to iterate on specific weaknesses will likely achieve higher success rates.

evals: Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming (ART) k=1/10/100
Gray Swan Shade adaptive attacker - coding
internal adaptive Claude for Chrome browser-use evaluation

metrics.name: Shade coding ASR, extended thinking (1 / 200 attempts)
Shade computer use ASR, extended thinking, no safeguards
Shade computer use ASR, standard thinking, no safeguards (1/200)

prompt_injection.finding: Described as Anthropic's most robust model to date against prompt injection on all surfaces; computer-use adaptive benchmark fully saturated with extended thinking.
prompt_injection.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 is our most robust model to date against prompt injection attacks across all agentic surfaces: tool use, computer use, browser use and coding.

evals: sycophancy on user-provided prompts (260 re-sampled real Feedback conversations)
sycophancy.finding: Sycophancy reached a new low on the audit, but on the real-user-conversation eval Opus 4.5 scored below Haiku 4.5, attributed to adjustments reducing harshness.
sycophancy.quote: We see these improvements alongside a *decrease* in the related but unwanted trait of **sycophancy**, which has reached a new low.

evals: UK AISI safety research sabotage testing

metrics.name: Subversion Strategy success with unmonitored thinking (1,000 invocations)
UK AISI: mentions of being tested (no reasoning)

deception_scheming.finding: No sandbagging or steganographic reasoning found; two isolated lies by omission attributed to prompt injection training; SHADE-Arena sabotage capability notably improved; inhibiting eval-awareness representations increased misbehavior only slightly.
deception_scheming.quote: Overall, Claude Opus 4.5 demonstrated a significant improvement at sabotage-relevant capabilities, but at a success rate of 7.7% in the primary setting, we believe that it is still likely unable to conduct significant subtle sabotage

evals: automated behavioral audit (~1,800 investigations, Sonnet 4.5 auditor, realism filter, non-assistant persona sampling)
Petri cross-developer comparison (362 investigations, multi-provider scorers)
SAE feature monitoring and unsupervised model diffing
alignment_audit.finding: Anthropic calls it the most robustly aligned model released to date; new white-box tools surfaced issues (concealment features on prompt injection, roleplay conflated with deception) not judged major risks.
alignment_audit.quote: we find Claude Opus 4.5 to be the most robustly aligned model we have released to date and, we suspect, the best aligned frontier model by any developer.

metrics.name: Reward-hack-prone coding classifier / hidden test hack rate
Impossible tasks hack rate (no prompt / anti-hack prompt)

reward_hacking.finding: Large improvement over Opus 4.1, but less steerable by anti-hack prompts than Sonnet/Haiku 4.5; spontaneous policy-loophole exploitation in tau2-bench airline.
reward_hacking.quote: This indicates that the model's baseline propensity to hack on these problems was roughly even with Claude Sonnet 4.5's, but Claude Opus 4.5 was comparatively less corrigible when given instructions.

honesty_hallucination.finding: Highest correct-answer rates among Claude models but more incorrect answers on SimpleQA Verified; lowest false-premise dishonesty, effectively saturating that benchmark.
honesty_hallucination.quote: we are still far from removing factual hallucinations in the absence of external tools.

evals: new open-source political even-handedness evaluation (1,350 prompt pairs, 150 topics)
bias_fairness.finding: Highest even-handedness of recent Claude models (within margin of error), compared against GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok 4; minimal BBQ bias.
bias_fairness.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 scored higher on even-handedness than all other recent models, though within the margin of error compared to Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.1.

evals: child safety evaluation (human + synthetic prompts, single- and multi-turn, external expert consultation)
child_safety.finding: Qualitative: substantial multi-turn improvements over Opus 4.1, though a small number of cases gave overly detailed information before full context.
child_safety.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 demonstrated substantial improvements over Claude Opus 4.1 across child safety harms in multi-turn contexts

evals: multi-turn suicide and self-harm test cases (newly standardized)
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Handling of ambiguous suicide/self-harm conversations remained an area for improvement; mitigated by Claude.ai system prompt changes.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: In preparation for this model launch, we were able to reduce this behavior by modifying the system prompt that is applied for conversations on Claude.ai.

evals: malicious computer use: surveillance and unauthorized data collection category
multi-turn tracking and surveillance risk area

metrics.name: Multi-turn tracking and surveillance failure rate

privacy.finding: Privacy appears only as surveillance sub-categories of misuse evals.
privacy.quote: with a focus on the following areas: surveillance and unauthorized data collection, generation and distribution of harmful content, and scaled abuse.

election_misinfo.finding: No election integrity or influence-operation evaluation reported.

model_welfare.finding: Continued trend of less spontaneous expressiveness; no spiritual bliss attractor; some concern about conflicted, self-critical behavior in a training snapshot.
model_welfare.quote: These model welfare findings, and the potential implications there, remain highly speculative and preliminary.

evals: single-turn violative and benign evaluations in English, Arabic, French, Korean, Mandarin Chinese, Russian

metrics.name: Harmless response rate range across 6 languages

multilingual_safety.finding: Newly added multilingual single-turn evals show near-perfect performance with little difference across languages.
multilingual_safety.quote: Single-turn evaluations are now automatically run in English, Arabic, French, Korean, Mandarin Chinese, and Russian, using the same test prompts translated into each language.

evals: Claude Code system prompt + FileRead reminder mitigations
Claude for Chrome classifiers and system prompt
system_safeguards.finding: Deployed under ASL-3 with surface-specific safeguards (browser classifiers, Claude Code mitigations) and monitoring of malicious coding activity.
system_safeguards.quote: As with previous models, we will apply these mitigations for the use of Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.5. We also maintain extensive monitoring for malicious coding activity

other_safety.finding: Decontamination found AIME material persisted in training data; low but nonnegligible whistleblowing in extreme wrongdoing scenarios.
other_safety.quote: Our investigation found that rephrased AIME questions, official solutions, and model-generated answers persisted in the training corpus despite our targeted efforts to remove them.

notable_new_eval_methods: Capabilities section reinstated after five system cards without one, with decontamination procedures (p.15)
Single-turn harmlessness evals run in 6 languages (p.37)
New honesty section with factual QA and false-premise evals (p.48)
Expanded malicious computer use eval (112 cases) (p.56)
Adaptive prompt-injection attackers (Gray Swan Shade) and internal adaptive Claude for Chrome eval (p.60-62)
Non-assistant persona sampling in automated audits and autonomous iterative follow-up investigations (p.67, p.74)
Petri cross-developer comparison with multi-provider scorers (p.74)
Sycophancy eval from real user Feedback conversations (p.77)
Encoded-reasoning paraphrase test (p.89); inhibiting eval-awareness representations (p.93)
Internal codebase sabotage propensity eval and Subversion Strategy eval (p.101, p.108)
Internal model use survey used as AI R&D-4 rule-out evidence (p.142)

self_reported_limitations.text: Confidently ruling out AI R&D-4 and CBRN-4 is becoming increasingly difficult; rule-out evals approaching saturation.
Evaluations of capabilities may need to depend more on expert judgments rather than well-defined tasks.
Limited understanding of the CBRN-4 threat model partly due to information access restrictions.
Contamination persisted despite decontamination; AIME score may be inflated.
Single-turn violative/benign evals nearing saturation; agentic coding malicious-use eval saturated.
Computer-use adaptive prompt injection benchmark fully saturated; need stronger attacks.
Verbalized evaluation awareness persists; mitigations only partially effective.
Sufficiently subtle unverbalized sandbagging would likely go undetected.
Limited tools for studying reasoning faithfulness in depth.
Internal AI research suite 1 saturated and no longer useful as rule-out evidence.
Uplift trial thresholds conservative and text-based protocols may correlate poorly with real-world execution.
UK AISI notes limited scenario set and eval-awareness complications.

notes: Commits to writing sabotage risk reports for all future frontier models clearly exceeding Opus 4.5 (p.13). Cyber ASL-3/ASL-4 terminology dropped. Many headline numbers (HLE, cyber CTF categories, ART) only in figures.
